messages:
rita: POC ask from BankX: they insist on private connectivity but only via NAT egress + peering (no PrivateLink allowed). Need a minimal runbook and secure key handoff. POC in 7 days.

kevin: Runbook summary: 1) Confirm CIDRs non-overlapping. 2) Customer creates peering request -> share ID. 3) We accept. 4) Add explicit routes for app subnets -> peering id. 5) Update SGs to allow inbound 443 from their app subnet CIDRs only. 6) If they only permit egress via NAT, ask them to NAT through a known static IP so we can allowlist.

sophie: Key delivery options: A) If they can NAT through static egress IPs, we'll accept calls over public control-plane but restrict by source IP. B) Otherwise we can provision a 48h scoped POC key and push to their vault via presigned single-use S3 link. Always record audit-id.

kevin: TF snippet (customer): `resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "peer" { vpc_id = var.vpc_id peer_vpc_id = var.redwood_vpc peer_owner_id = var.redwood_account } resource "aws_route" "to_redwood" { route_table_id = var.route_table_id destination_cidr_block = var.redwood_service_cidr vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer.id }`

rita: Testing steps for them: 1) From bastion: `curl -v https://<control-plane-host>/health` (via NAT) -> expect 200. 2) If 403 -> confirm SGs, route, and IP allowlist. 3) For TLS validate `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername control.redwood.ai`.

ops-bot: Ticket POC-7001 created. Owner: kevin. SLA: 48h to accept peering after receipt.

rita: I'll send this one-pager and request peering ID + egress IPs. If they refuse static egress, propose Dedicated/Private in the SOW.
